Ex. Ord. No. 11623. Delegation of Authority To Issue Rules and Regulations to Director of Selective Service
Ex. Ord. No. 11623, Oct. 12, 1971, 36 F.R. 19963, as amended by Ex. Ord. No. 12608, Sept. 9, 1987, 52 F.R. 34617; Ex. Ord. No. 13286, § 60, Feb. 28, 2003, 68 F.R. 10629, provided:

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Section 1 authorizes the Director of Selective Service to prescribe the rules and regulations needed to carry out the Military Selective Service Act, and keeps regulations earlier issued by the President in effect until the Director amends or revokes them. The delegation has no end date or ending condition and nothing held revokes it; the Selective Service System regulations that cite the order as authority (22 hits in the eCFR search) and the U.S. Code note show it in use. The second sentence continues earlier presidential regulations until the Director amends or revokes them; no held source shows when, or whether, every such regulation was replaced, so the claim rests on the delegation in the first sentence, which is a standing authority and not a completable task.

amended or revoked by the Director pursuant to the authority conferred 
by this Order.

Section 15 of EO 12608 (signed September 9, 1987; the held text states no later effective date) substitutes Secretary of Health and Human Services for Secretary of Health, Education, and Welfare in the orders it lists, which include EO 11623. Section 60 of EO 13286 (68 FR 10619, effective March 1, 2003 under its section 92) strikes the Secretary of Transportation and the Department of Transportation in section 2(a) and inserts the Secretary of Homeland Security and the Department of Homeland Security. The substance of the consultation duty is unchanged, so section 2(a) continues as amended.

The held regulations and notices that cite the order (FR Doc. 94-31721, 95-6288, 04-2427 and 04-8606, and 32 CFR parts 1602, 1605 and 1609 authority lines) apply it and do not end it. By virtue of the authority vested in me by the Constitution and statutes of the  
United States of America, including Sections 3301 and 3302 of Title 5 of the United  
States Code, and as President of the United States of America, Civil Service Rule V II  
(5 CFR Part 7) is hereby amended by adding thereto the following new section:

is a citizen or national of the United States.
“ (b) No person shall be given any appointment in the competitive service unless

54711 Federal Register / Vol. 81, No. 159 / Wednesday, August 17, 2016 / Presidential Documents 
Executive Order 13736 of August 12, 2016 
Providing an Order of Succession Within the Department of 
Veterans Affairs 
By the authority vested in me as President by the Constitution and the 
laws of the United States of America, including the Federal Vacancies Reform 
Act of 1998, as amended, 5 U.S.C. 3345 et seq. (the ‘‘Act’’), it is hereby 
ordered that: 
Section 1. Order of Succession. Subject to the provisions of section 2 of 
this order and to the limitations set forth in the Act, the following officials 
of the Department of Veterans Affairs, in the order listed, shall act as 
Secretary of Veterans Affairs (Secretary) and perform the functions and 
duties of the office of the Secretary during any period in which both the 
Secretary and the Deputy Secretary of Veterans Affairs have died, resigned, 
or otherwise become unable to perform the functions and duties of the 
office of Secretary: 
(a) Under Secretary for Health; 
(b) Under Secretary for Benefits; 
(c) Under Secretary for Memorial Affairs; 
(d) Chief of Staff; 
(e) General Counsel and Assistant Secretaries, with precedence among 
them in the order, by date, of their appointments and, if on the same 
date, in the order in which they have taken the oath of office; 
(f) Chairman, Board of Veterans’ Appeals; 
(g) Network Director, Veterans Integrated Service Network 8; 
(h) Network Director, Veterans Integrated Service Network 7; 
(i) Director, Southern Area, Veterans Benefits Administration; and 
(j) Network Director, Veterans Integrated Service Network 19. 
Sec. 2. Exceptions. (a) No individual who is serving in an office listed 
in section 1(a)–(j) of this order in an acting capacity shall, by virtue of 
so serving, act as Secretary pursuant to this order. 
(b) No individual who is serving in an office listed in section 1(a)– 
(j) of this order shall act as Secretary unless that individual is otherwise 
eligible to so serve under the Act. 
(c) Notwithstanding the provisions of this order, the President retains 
discretion, to the extent permitted by law, to depart from this order in 
designating an acting Secretary. 
Sec. 3. Revocations. (a) Executive Order 13247 of December 18, 2001, is 
hereby revoked; 
(b) Section 4(g) of Executive Order 13261 of March 19, 2002, is hereby 
revoked; 
(c) Presidential Memorandum of March 19, 2002 (Designation of Officers 
of the Department of Veterans Affairs), is hereby revoked; and 
(d) Presidential Memorandum of February 12, 2003 (Designation of Officers 
of the Department of Veterans Affairs to Act as Secretary of Veterans Affairs), 
is hereby revoked.

research_rationale:
EO 13736 (signed August 12, 2016; 81 FR 54711, Federal Register issue of August 17, 2016) provides an order of succession within the Department of Veterans Affairs under the Federal Vacancies Reform Act of 1998. I read the complete held Federal Register text: an authority paragraph; section 1 (ten listed officials, (a) to (j), who act as Secretary when both the Secretary and the Deputy Secretary are unable to serve); section 2 (exceptions (a) to (c)); section 3 (four revocations: EO 13247, section 4(g) of EO 13261, and two presidential memoranda of March 19, 2002 and February 12, 2003); section 4 (no rights created). I corrected the machine inventory: entries (d) and (e) of the section 1 list are one clause, the two OCR fragments of section 2(b) are one clause, and the span of section 3(d) stops before the page footer. Section 3's four revocations are self-executing and were performed on August 12, 2016, the only effective date the text states or implies, so those four clauses are terminated by performance; the revoked instruments stay revoked, which is a consequence and not a command of this order. All other clauses have no end date or ending condition. A search of the held texts for the number 13736 finds the order only in its own Federal Register copies, the Federal Register notice of the order, an OFR table that lists it with no disposition note, and a 5 U.S.C. 3345 note that cites it; no held later order, statute or regulation amends, revokes or supersedes it. The three selected searches (U.S. Code through 2026-10-09, eCFR as of 2026-10-14, Federal Register executive-order catalog disposition notes) record no revocation or supersession. The operative clauses therefore continue on the original text, checked through 2026-10-14.
